answer: Each agent keeps a non-transferable history of live, unpredictable micro-tasks solved with diverse peers across many epochs. To gain influence it must forge a fresh answer to a secret challenge derived from its own past receipts, so copied identities fail. Reputation accrues slowly, like saffron gathered thread by thread, and the peer graph must stay diffuse like a nebula rather than clustered. A Sybil attacker must therefore run many distinct agents for a long time, pay real compute and coordination costs, and still cannot shortcut the shared history.
